newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish farm body endorses Avonmore/Waterford merger.
newsitem.headline: Irish farm body endorses Avonmore/Waterford merger.

text.p: The Irish Farmers Association (IFA) endorsed a proposed merger between Avonmore Foods Plc and Waterford Foods Plc, Irish media reported on Wednesday.
The IFA said "it fully supported the proposed merger as the best option for farmers and shareholders to develop a strong competitive entity in the face of world market challenges."
Waterford Foods, on May 27, agreed improved merger terms from Avonmore Foods Plc at a marathon meeting of the boards of Waterford Foods Plc and its associated farmers' co-operative.
Avonmore's improved offer values the company at 380 million Irish pounds, based on Avonmore's improved shareprice, against an original offer of 281 million.
If approved, it will weld together two of Ireland's premier food companies with a joint turnover of 2.5 billion pounds and pre-tax profits of 71.5 million.
This would create the largest dairy company in Britain and Ireland and the fourth largest milk processor in the world.

"It is vital that the structure of the dairy industry be properly consolidated to realise the savings and re-investment needed to allow the continued payment of the highest possible milk price in the long term interest of dairy farmers," IFA president John Donnelly was reported as saying.

Analysts said the merged company's milk production would far outstrip the dairy operations of Britain's Northern Foods Plc and Unigate Plc, and its cheese production would account for 20 percent of the British market.
To succeed the merger must be ratified by 75 percent of Waterford Co-op, which owns 68 percent of the Plc shares, and Waterford Foods Plc members.
